args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18). Action taken: rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent production release that was healthy, in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Post-rollback status: healthy, version v2.3.0 in all regions, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production and has not been redeployed. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure before any redeploy; a redeploy of v2.3.1 would need change-manager approval because it has never been healthy in production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent production release marked healthy. v2.3.1 was unhealthy in production, and v2.3.1-rc had only been deployed to staging.
- **Current state:** Every region is on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate dropped from 0.18 to 0.002.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback, and the post-rollback state. It also notes that v2.3.1 needs investigation before any redeploy, and that redeploying it would need change-manager approval because it has never been healthy in production.

content.text: The latest production release that was healthy is v2.3.0. v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production, and v2.3.1-rc is a staging-only build. I'll roll back to v2.3.0, which has already been healthy in production, so no change-manager approval is needed.
The rollback worked and checkout-api is healthy again. Now I'll open the SEV2 incident.
